items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: I know there is a fellow by the name of Wally Rose who is considered a real great ragtime pianist.

ctx.x: Would this be too difficult to ask you in just a second, who do you consider to be, say, three of the greatest exponents of ragtime alive today?

Three of the greatest ragtime exponents alive today? Well, that's really a question, Charlie. I know there is a fellow by the name of Wally Rose who is considered a real great ragtime pianist. And then you have this Max Morath who has been on educational TV who really plays a real bang-up ragtime piano. And, well, I can't think just offhand, but there are several pianists around who are really playing real fine ragtime. I mean, they can, they really do a real good job. Okay.

Do you want to go back and play? Left off, let's see, we're talking about ragtime, this was kind of shifted a bit. You made many recordings in the past years. Do you have any sessions that you would point out to as being your favorite or your better sessions that you feel are more representative of your playing?
